newsitem.title: TAIWAN: United Micro limit up on huge investment.
newsitem.headline: United Micro limit up on huge investment.

text.p: Taiwan's chipmaker United Microelectronics surged at mid-morning on Friday after announcing a T$500 billion, 10-year wafer fabrication project on Thursday, brokers said.

The project, Taiwan's single biggest investment scheme to date, called for the completion of six advanced eight- and 12-inch fabrication plants in the island's burgeoning southern science park over a 10-year span.
After 65 minutes, at 0205 GMT, United Microelectronics was up the daily seven percent limit to T$103. Its rival Taiwan Semiconductor was also limit up to T$111.5.
In April, Taiwan Semiconductor said it would launch a T$400 billion wafer project in Taiwan over a 10-year span.

"Such huge investment projects by United Microelectronics and Taiwan Semiconductor lead investors to believe that Taiwan's hope is in high-tech electronics industry investments," said independent analyst Michael Hung.
"Investors think if those firms were not bullish on their outlook, they would not launch such huge schemes," he said.
Hung said investors still were buying electronics with confidence despite seeing sectoral price-earnings ratios rise from around 20 to about 30, about the overall market's average.
Such high P/Es had been seen as too risky.
Hung forecast United Microelectronics' earnings per share at T$2.76 in 1997 and T$4.14 in 1998. A P/E ratio of 30 would point to a reasonable market price of T$82.8 to T$124.2.
He forecast Taiwan Semiconductor's earnings per share at T$3.9 in 1997 and T$5.5 in 1998, which would translate into a market price of T$117 to T$165 at a P/E of 30.
"Since the firms' huge investments are 10-year plans, their longterm outlook might be even better," Hung said.
